rationales: Robert Hooke described cells, but did not discover the nucleus.
Laveran is known for discovering the malaria parasite, not the cell nucleus.
Robert Brown discovered the cell nucleus in 1831.
Louis Pasteur is known for work on microorganisms and pasteurization, not the nucleus.
Anopheles mosquitoes transmit human malaria, not the malaria commonly described in sparrows.
Dengue is a disease, not a mosquito genus that spreads malaria in sparrows.
Aedes mosquitoes transmit diseases such as dengue, not sparrow malaria.
Culex mosquitoes spread malaria among sparrows.
Cell membranes are mainly composed of lipids and proteins.
Cholesterol is a membrane component but is not its main composition by itself.
Lignin is found in plant cell walls, not as the main component of cell membranes.
Chitin is found in fungal cell walls and arthropod exoskeletons, not as the main membrane component.
Margulis and Schwartz proposed a later five-kingdom scheme, but the standard five-kingdom classification is credited to Whittaker.
Torn Efort is not credited with introducing the five-kingdom classification.
Robert Whittaker introduced the five-kingdom classification in 1969.
Ernst Haeckel proposed a three-kingdom classification, not the five-kingdom system.
Goitre is commonly caused by iodine deficiency.
Osteoarthritis is a joint disorder and is not caused by protein deficiency.
Marasmus results from severe deficiency of calories and protein.
Colour blindness is usually inherited and is not caused by protein deficiency.
Arteries generally do not have valves along their length to prevent backflow.
Capillaries have no valves.
The rectum is part of the digestive system and has no blood-flow valves.
Veins contain valves that help prevent the backward flow of blood.
200–250 grams is below the usual textbook range for an adult human heart.
150–200 grams is generally too low for a normal adult human heart.
A normal adult human heart weighs approximately 250–350 grams.
100–200 grams is generally too low for a normal adult human heart.
Volvox consists of cells living together in a colony.
Amoeba is a single-celled organism, not a colony.
A frog is a multicellular organism with tissue-level organization, not colonial organization.
Mustard is a multicellular plant, not a colonial organism.
A good hypothesis should be consistent with the available data.
A good hypothesis must be testable.
A hypothesis need not already be correct; it is tested to determine whether it is supported.
A good hypothesis should make predictions that can be tested.
Protista is not the kingdom assigned to bacteria in the traditional five-kingdom classification.
Bacteria are assigned to Kingdom Monera in the traditional five-kingdom classification.
Fungi are organisms such as yeasts and mushrooms, not bacteria.
Plantae contains plants, not bacteria.
Chakor is a national bird of Pakistan, not its national animal.
Ibex is not Pakistan’s designated national animal.
Urial is not Pakistan’s designated national animal.
Markhor is the national animal of Pakistan.
Fungi generally have cell walls made mainly of chitin.
Algae generally possess cell walls.
Animal cells lack cell walls.
Plant cells generally have cell walls made mainly of cellulose.
Robert Hooke used a microscope and coined the term “cell,” but did not develop the first microscope.
Zacharias Janssen is commonly credited with developing the first compound microscope.
Louis Pasteur was a microbiologist, not the developer of the first microscope.
Robert Brown discovered the nucleus, not the first microscope.
Spindle fibers are already formed by metaphase, when chromosomes align at the cell equator.
Interphase is when the cell grows and replicates DNA; the mitotic spindle forms later.
G₂ is part of interphase, before spindle formation during mitosis.
Spindle fibers begin to form during prophase.
Enzymes are generally proteins made of amino-acid chains.
Minerals are not the structural building blocks of enzymes.
Vitamins may assist enzyme activity but do not form the enzyme’s protein structure.
Fats are not the structural building blocks of enzymes.
